evidence.quote: | Ready, Some books when not (books.Books.Customers.IsEmpty && books.Books.Drafts.IsEmpty && books.Books.Invoices.IsEmpty && books.Payments.IsEmpty) ->

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Every new rule is in Tier 2. Summa.Storage.Transfer owns the file format, the refusal order and the data-version check, and it reuses LocalSnapshot and Exports. The engine owns the 'new books only' guard, the GitHub and files-pack refusals and the notice. The only Tier 3 change (AccountingWire) maps kernel event names to engine messages and decides nothing. app/index.html only binds view values and events.

evidence.quote: match Transfer.export manifest books ctx.Now with

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effect is performed or read below Tier 4. The time comes in through ctx.Now. The download and the save are returned as engine effects (OfferDownload, and SaveBooks through save) for the edge to carry out. Transfer.export and Transfer.read are deterministic and can be tested without effects. One caveat: Transfer.fs is a Tier 2 module and uses System.IO.MemoryStream and System.Text.Json (Utf8JsonWriter, JsonDocument). That breaks the instance symbol rule ARC-SYM-01, but it is in-memory serialization, not an effect, so it does not lower this effect-flow score.

evidence.quote: match LocalSnapshot.encode manifest r, Exports.dataVersion r with
| false, _, _ -> { model with Error = Some "This browser cannot offer downloads here." }, []

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The facts this change uses (the classification, the data version, the snapshot encoding and checks, the business date) all come from their existing authorities, not from new copies. Schema, Version and NotATransferFile are each defined once. The only restated literal is the existing user-facing message 'This browser cannot offer downloads here.', which matches the earlier one; it is a message, not a domain fact.

evidence.quote: | [], Ok _ when fileVersion >= 2 && statedContents root <> Some(contents restored.Books) ->

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The rule for what the books hold, the version 1/2 acceptance and the contents check are all in Summa.Storage (Tier 2). The preview is built in the engine (Tier 2) from Transfer.read and Transfer.contents. There is no Tier 3 change. app/index.html only binds booksTransferPreview.

evidence.quote: | BooksTransferTextChanged v -> { model with BooksTransferText = v; BooksTransferPreview = transferPreview v }, []

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect. The preview is computed purely in the engine's transition and returns no effects. Import still saves through the existing SaveBooks effect. As in change set 1, Transfer.fs keeps using System.Text.Json in Tier 2 (ARC-SYM-01 symbol concern), but this is in-memory parsing, not an effect.

evidence.quote: match v.TryGetInt32() with | true, n -> n <> 1 && n <> Version | _ -> true

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The counts have one authority, Transfer.contents, which export, read and the preview all use. Two facts are restated, though the copies agree. First, the 'export's UTC date' derivation is copied into transferPreview; it repeats the expression already in the BooksTransferImported notice. Second, the oldest readable version is a bare literal 1 beside the Version constant, not a named definition.
